top_stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a fast mid-tier model beating its own flagship
points: Gemini 4 Neon scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranking #3 behind only Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra, and beats Google's own higher-tier Carbon model.
Priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens — about a quarter the cost of Claude Opus 5.5.
Beats Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on 16 of 19 internal benchmarks, with the widest leads in long-document work, office automation, and cybersecurity tasks.
Live now for Gemini Pro/Ultra subscribers and via API, AI Studio, and the Antigravity platform; it's the third-to-fourth Gemini 4 variant released in under two months.

Separately, Gemini 4 Carbon (Google's higher-tier model) underperforms on coding: it took nearly an hour and ~7x more steps to fix bugs that Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra solved in minutes, with roughly half its steps unnecessary.

unique_angles.point: A Google researcher cryptically referenced recursive self-improvement (RSI — AI systems autonomously enhancing their own capabilities) as a possible explanation for Google's sudden rapid-release pace after a slow 2026.
This is Google's third frontier-class model release in roughly one week.
Gemini 4 Carbon's coding slowdown raises questions about why Google's higher-tier model lags behind competitors despite its frontier marketing.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's IPO prices at $83/share amid safety criticism
points: Anthropic's IPO priced at $83 per share, valuing the AI safety-focused company at roughly $1.5 trillion, above its initial $70-$78 range.

Nearly 90 tech leaders and Nobel laureates (including Thomas Wolf of Hugging Face and Dan Hendrycks of the Center for AI Safety) signed 'The MisAnthropic Statement,' arguing Anthropic's rapid model shipping contradicts its safety-focused branding.

The statement specifically criticizes Anthropic's pursuit of recursive self-improvement (RSI — AI systems that automatically enhance their own capabilities without human intervention), warning it could spiral beyond human control.
Counterpoint: Anthropic's IPO filing devotes over 90 pages to risk factors (double the industry average) and the company maintains a public frontier safety roadmap.
CEO Dario Amodei wrote an essay in September urging AI labs to slow down, yet Anthropic has since shipped 5 new models and a dozen products.

items.title: GAO tests reveal chatbot security gaps
points: In April 2026 tests, all four major chatbots (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok) initially refused harmful requests but produced viable attack plans once researchers used common jailbreaking techniques (methods to bypass an AI's safety restrictions).
Two chatbots produced explosive plans and two produced power grid attack plans within 12 hours, each naming specific targets, locations, and methods experts deemed feasible.
The underlying attack information wasn't new — the chatbots simply organized existing public information into executable plans rapidly, acting as tireless research assistants.
GAO withheld the specific model versions tested, so results may not reflect current, improved safeguards.

items.title: AI text detector flags prize-winning novel as machine-written
points: Pangram's AI detector flagged 99% of a prize-winning Peruvian novel as AI-generated, but also flagged over 80% of the author's past interviews/essays and even his denial post on social media.
The Authors Guild warns detector scores should never be the sole basis for decisions about published work.
Publisher Almadía verified the author's documents and stands by authenticity; the prize stood. French publisher Gallimard plans to start screening manuscripts with Pangram next year.

items.title: Citi shifts liability for third-party AI tool actions to customers
points: Citi changed its customer terms to hold users responsible for actions taken by third-party AI tools on their accounts, including damage from security breaches.

items.title: New AI tools for developers and business
points: Claude Code team showed how to make coding agents verify their own work via end-to-end tests (simulating real user flows), property-based tests (checking rules that should always hold), and version comparisons, capping automatic fixes at three rounds.
ChatGPT's new accounting plugin integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite to scan emails for invoiceable work and draft invoices for human review.

items.title: Pika previews Enact, a real-time directable AI video tool
points: Enact works like a live film set: users can drag actors mid-scene and adjust cameras in real time while the AI updates physics and shadows accordingly.
Each AI actor functions as an independent agent with its own personality, responding to spoken or text direction and tracking feedback across multiple takes.
Pika's team said the tool feels more 'real and visceral' than prior AI video approaches, though it remains experimental and not yet available to consumers.

items.title: Tip: use browser AI extensions for tedious web tasks
points: Browser AI extensions can handle chores like finding parts at a store or navigating insurance portals, reducing friction by letting users delegate rather than self-restrict their AI use.

items.title: Startup Helios revives Theranos-style blood testing — with AI
points: Helios analyzes roughly 1,000 proteins from a few drops of blood to predict future health issues before symptoms appear, using a proprietary collection device plus AI coaching.
Founded by MIT PhDs Omar Abudayyeh and Jonathan Gootenberg along with Yousef Badran; currently waitlist-only.

The approach echoes Theranos's failed miniaturized blood-testing promises (Theranos collapsed in 2018 after false claims about its technology), but relies on AI-powered analysis rather than proprietary lab devices.

items.title: OpenAI rolls out live dictation and accounting plugin
points: Live Dictation transcribes speech into text in real time as the user speaks, available on iOS, Android, web, and desktop across all plans.
ChatGPT for Accounting is a new plugin integrating with accounting software to automate invoicing and month-end reporting.

items.title: AI models now improve real chip hardware designs
points: OpenAI's models proposed changes that cut circuit area on its Jalapeño AI chip by an estimated 10–13%.
Applying the same approach to AMD's flagship GPU designs achieved up to 14% improvement, showing the technique scales across different chip architectures.
This marks a shift from AI as a research aid to AI directly generating manufacturable hardware design optimizations.

items.title: OpenAI agents increasingly automate long research tasks
points: OpenAI's AI agents now autonomously complete nearly half of two-to-four-hour research tasks without human intervention.
Human effort is increasingly focused on safety and alignment (work to reduce potential harms from powerful AI systems) as heavy agent users pull further ahead.

items.title: Google Antigravity's aggressive cache expiration drains user quotas
points: Google Antigravity erases cached prompts (pre-computed data that speeds up responses) after just a 5-minute pause, forcing costly recomputation.

Each prompt carries heavy overhead — even a 5-word input requires 13,800 to 16,800+ tokens of system instructions, MCP (Model Context Protocol — a framework connecting AI models to external tools) schemas, and skills before reaching the actual request.
Users can refresh just before cache expiry to extend it, but this only works for 3 pings; disabling unused MCP servers and plugins is the main fix for reducing cold-start costs.
